title: Controllable Data Generation by Deep Learning: A Review
summary: Surveys techniques for generating data whose properties can be controlled, organised by when the control signal enters the process: before generation, by concatenating the target properties onto the generator input or mapping them into latent space; after it, by optimising the sample in latent or data space; and during training, by goal-oriented rewards or by biasing the training distribution. It then standardises the evaluation metrics for data quality and property controllability and surveys the benchmark datasets used in molecule design, protein design, image editing, text style transfer and emotional speech. CTGAN enters the taxonomy as a pre-generation property-concatenation model, cited for feeding the conditional vector into both the generator and the discriminator; the mechanism is described and classified, not run.
evidence: Table 1 places reference 112, the CTGAN paper, in the cell Controllable generation from scratch / Pre-generation control / Property concatenation; section 3.1.1 cites it among the works that feed handcrafted properties into the generator of a GAN and, in the same citation group, into the discriminator so that D(x) is rewritten D(x|c); CTGAN is never named in prose and no experiment in the survey uses it

title: Diffusion Models for Tabular Data Imputation and Synthetic Data Generation
summary: Proposes MTabGen, a diffusion model for mixed-type tabular data that makes three changes to TabDDPM: an encoder-decoder transformer replaces the MLP denoiser, the conditioning features reach the decoder through the attention mechanism as key and value rather than by adding their embedding to the masked features, and the split between conditioned and masked columns is redrawn per row during training, so one model covers both synthetic data generation and missing-value imputation. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five generative baselines it is measured against across ten datasets, run from the SDV distribution and tuned under the same Bayesian search budget as the diffusion models.
evidence: section 5.2 lists CTGAN and TVAE among the synthetic data generation baselines and footnote 3 states that the implementation used for both is the one provided at sdv.dev; Table 2 reports their ML efficiency on ten datasets, Table A2 gives their hyperparameter search space, and Table B1 compares their training and sampling cost

title: On the Gap Between Diffusion and Transformer Multi-Tabular Generation
summary: Asks why a transformer relational synthesiser trails a diffusion one on multi-table data when the two are close on single tables, and attributes the difference to how each represents contextual information and the parent-child link. Two changes close much of the gap: tying the transformer block weights of the parent model to the relational adapter's decoder so only the child vocabulary is fine-tuned, and inserting a cluster identifier as an in-context categorical cue in both tables, an autoregressive stand-in for classifier guidance. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the single-table baselines it benchmarks, and CTGAN is described as the GAN adaptation that handles heterogeneous columns and class imbalance.
evidence: Table 1 reports CTGAN and TVAE on machine learning efficiency, discriminator measure and training time across five single-table datasets; section 2 states that CTGAN builds on the GAN architecture to work with heterogeneous data and handle class imbalance; section 1 names TVAE and CTGAN as the VAE and GAN approaches the field followed before graph and diffusion methods

title: GAN_BERT: An Advanced Neural Architecture for Effective Fraud Detection on Imbalanced Datasets
summary: Proposes GAN_BERT, a three-stage pipeline for credit-card fraud detection on a dataset where fraud is a fifth of a percent of rows: CTGAN is trained on the minority class alone to produce synthetic fraud records, a stratified loader mixes real majority, real minority and synthetic rows into balanced batches at configurable ratios, and a FinBERT classifier is fine-tuned on those batches. CTGAN is run unmodified as the generator stage, with the conditional generator and discriminator objectives reproduced from the CTGAN paper, so the named model is a composite built around CTGAN rather than a variant of it; the reported precision and recall gains on the minority class rest on the rows it supplies.
evidence: section 3.1, headed Synthetic Data Generation via Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks, states that the generator learns the conditional distribution p(x|c) of the minority set and cites reference 20, the CTGAN paper, for the adversarial setup; Figure 1 places the CTGAN module ahead of the data loader and Figure 2 shows its embedding layer applying conditional filters; section 3.2 defines the synthetic-to-real batch ratio r_syn; no modification to CTGAN itself is described anywhere in the methodology

title: Just-in-Time Logic Enforcement
summary: Argues that domain rules should constrain a language model while it generates rather than during training or after inference, and demonstrates LeJIT, which interleaves an SMT solver into token-by-token decoding: before each token the solver instantiates the active rules with the values produced so far, computes the feasible range for the current variable, and prunes tokens from which no compliant completion exists, with a character-level transition system bridging the model's tokens and the solver's variables. A generic GPT-2 guided this way reaches parity with task-specific systems on network telemetry imputation and on synthetic trace generation while satisfying every extracted rule. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five generators it is measured against on the generation task.
evidence: section 4.2 lists CTGAN and TVAE, both reference 53, among the synthetic network data generators compared against; Figure 5 reports their Jensen-Shannon divergence against the original distribution for six measurement fields alongside NetShare, E-WGAN-GP and REaLTabFormer

title: Tabular Data Augmentation for Machine Learning: Progress and Prospects of Embracing Generative AI
summary: Reviews tabular data augmentation for machine learning as a three-stage pipeline: pre-augmentation, covering eight table preparation tasks from error handling to entity matching; augmentation, split into retrieval-based methods that fetch data from external table pools and generation-based methods that synthesise it, each subdivided by whether it acts at the row, column, cell or table level; and post-augmentation, covering datasets, metrics, evaluation policies and optimisation strategies. CTGAN is the survey's representative class-imbalance-aware record generator, described by its conditional generator and training-by-sampling strategy, recommended in the practical-guidelines table for class-imbalance scenarios, and cited as the source of the statistical-fidelity comparison used to judge synthetic tables; nothing is run.
evidence: section 4.2.1 states CTGAN employs a conditional generator with a training-by-sampling strategy to balance discrete attributes; Table 9 recommends CTGAN for the class-imbalance scenario; section 5.2 cites it for the statistical comparison of original and synthetic distributions; Table 4 lists it under content-based table representation; the survey runs no experiments

title: Tabular Generative Model with Graph-Theoretical Methodologies toward Effective Financial Fraud Detection
summary: Argues that fraud-detection tables defeat general tabular generators through extreme class imbalance, sparsity and many non-normal attributes, and proposes three graph-theoretical generative models for them, SeparateGGM, SignedGGM and HybridGGM, which build class-wise and signed K-NN graphs over the data, derive centrality indicators from them, and turn those into a per-instance influence score; the paper also finds the K ratios that maximise the graph measurements coincide with the best detection accuracy, reducing hyperparameter search to graph analysis. CTGAN is the base generative model the method extends: the influence scores are inserted into CTGAN's critic and generator objectives, SDV supplies the implementation that is run, and CTGAN and TVAE are also two of the seven baselines the result is measured against.
evidence: footnote 9 states CTGAN is adopted as the base model in the approach since it shows the best accuracy; section 4.6.1 extends the critic and generator loss functions of the original CTGAN with the graph-centrality influence scores; section 6.1 sets the base model's pac size to 11, batch size 256 and 500 epochs and implements CTGAN and TVAE with SDV 1.11.0; section 3.2 credits CTGAN's mode-specific preprocessing for handling per-feature multi-modality; Tables 4-7 report CTGAN and TVAE among the seven baselines
